day_trading/wm_fix_reversal.notes: Researcher-designed: fades the WM/Reuters 4pm London fix volatility spike on EURUSD.r/GBPUSD.r. v1 (fixed MinSpikeSizePips=12, kept for comparison) looked strong but its out-of-sample trade frequency collapsed ~85-90% (EURUSD zero trades in 2023). v2 redesign replaced the fixed threshold with a volatility-adaptive one (MinSpikeVsAvgMultiplier=2.0 x rolling 20-day average of the fix window's own recent moves, 5-pip floor) -- fixed frequency collapse decisively but the larger, honest OOS sample (158 trades) revealed a thin edge: PF 1.06 (EUR) / 1.04 (GBP) OOS, comparable to london_range_fade's own ~1.05-1.14. Parked 2026-09-22, briefly set to live_candidate on the user's direct instruction (overriding Researcher's assessment), then tested the one open thread that might have justified it: built v2_portfolio/ (combined EUR+GBP one-account harness) to check whether each pair's non-coinciding losing OOS years meant a diversification benefit. RESULT: hypothesis failed -- combined-account drawdown is WORSE than either pair alone in both periods (in-sample 14.56-15.44% vs 8.7-10.2% individually, came within half a point of the 15% kill-switch; out-of-sample 9.11-9.67% vs 6.9-7.6%), because 24% of days both pairs traded saw BOTH lose simultaneously (same fix event, correlated risk) -- see v2_portfolio/review.md. RE-PARKED by user 2026-09-22 after seeing this result -- not discarded/rejected, just not being actively iterated on for now. See strategies/day_trading/wm_fix_reversal/STRATEGY.md, v2/review.md, v2/comparison.md, v2_portfolio/review.md.

scalping/overlap_momentum_scalp.notes: User-requested: scalping strategy during the London/New York overlap (13:00-16:00 London), EURUSD.r, M1. Four variants tested, 2021-2023 in-sample / 2024-2025 out-of-sample: v1 momentum continuation (PF 0.73, ~49% WR, hit 15% kill-switch), v2 momentum fade -- opposite direction, same signal (PF 0.60, ~45% WR, also hit kill-switch, confirming the single-bar signal carries no real directional info either way), v3 deviation-from-SMA fade at default params (PF 0.82, but win rate 55.86% -- real signal, R:R just miscalibrated; a 7-combo SL/TP sweep showed win rate and reward trading off in lockstep, PF stuck 0.82-0.89 regardless -- signature of costs/geometry dominating), v3 tuned/locked (higher selectivity threshold) -- diagnosed gross price P&L was actually POSITIVE (+$729.60/725 trades) but commission (-$1,784.13) was 2.4x the edge and wiped it out; raising selectivity got in-sample PF to 1.02 (221 trades) but 2 of 3 years were individually negative, entire result carried by one year -- out-of-sample confirmed this was a small-sample artifact: PF 0.80, -$371 net. Decisive rejection across multiple well-motivated angles, same pattern as london_orb. Moved to strategies/_graveyard/overlap_momentum_scalp/. See REASON.md for full detail and what would need to be true to revisit (lower-commission venue, true order-flow data, or accepting a longer non-scalping holding horizon).

scalping/overlap_deviation_scalp.notes: Direct continuation of overlap_momentum_scalp (user instructed 'keep going until you make one, no need to wait for approval' after that line was discarded). Reused its one validated mechanism (deviation-from-SMA fade) and tested it exhaustively across every reasonable lever: direction (fade confirmed correct vs continuation, twice), bar granularity (M1 vs M5), symbol (GBPUSD/GBPJPY/EURUSD/USDJPY -- USDJPY never fit, PF 0.41), selectivity threshold (found real non-monotonic peaks), hold time (fixed a real design flaw -- 68-73% of trades were hitting an arbitrary 15-min cutoff before reaching target; 30-min peak identified, quintupled net profit in-sample), session width (full London session beat the overlap alone), and volume confirmation (added no value). 13 combinations tested total. Best result (v4, GBPUSD.r, M5, full London session): in-sample PF 1.09 on 1230 trades with every year individually profitable and win rate stable within 1pt across 3 years -- but out-of-sample PF 0.81 on 727 trades, win rate dropped 4-5pts. Both the in-sample success and out-of-sample failure are large-sample, statistically confident results, not noise -- the strongest, most conclusive negative finding of the whole scalping investigation. Same regime-dependence pattern seen in gotobi/wm_fix_reversal (strong 2021-2023, weaker 2024-2025) but sharper here -- the micro-edge appears to have genuinely diminished rather than just weakened. See REASON.md for full 13-combination table and what would need to be true to revisit (lower-commission venue, real order-flow data, or a volatility-regime filter that resolves the tension between trading often enough to overcome fixed costs and only trading when the regime supports the edge).

scalping/liquidity_sweep_reversal.notes: Built after deep external research per user's 'think out of the box' instruction (previous two scalping lines, 17 combinations, both discarded). A structurally different signal from everything tried before: fades a wick that sweeps through a recent swing high/low and closes back inside the prior range (documented liquidity-grab/stop-hunt pattern, based on concrete price structure, not a statistical rolling-average threshold). GBPUSD.r, M5, full London session. 8-combination sweep across SwingLookback (12/20/30) and MinSweepPips (2/4/6): PF plateaued at 0.86-0.95 across every combination, never crossing 1.0 -- no in-sample result worth validating out-of-sample. External research conducted alongside this (cited in REASON.md) confirms the broader conclusion is well-supported, not just internal trial and error: FX majors aren't reliably cointegrated (rules out pairs trading), triangular arbitrage needs sub-millisecond multi-broker infrastructure retail doesn't have, genuine order-flow-based FX predictability is real but academically documented as fragile against transaction costs, and MT5 tick volume isn't real volume. Across 25+ backtested configurations total (this strategy plus the two prior scalping lines), no signal tested got anywhere near the 60-75% win rate the literature says retail scalping needs to overcome realistic costs. CONCLUSION: scalping does not appear currently viable on this account with MT5-derivable data: no Level 2/order-flow data, standard retail commission structure. Recommend directing further effort to day-trading timescales (where gotobi already found a real edge) rather than continuing to search for a scalping edge. See REASON.md for full detail and research citations.

day_trading/intraday_momentum_carry.notes: Built per user's 'go for day trading' instruction, directly implementing a published peer-reviewed finding (Gao/Han/Li/Zhou 2018 JFE: first half-hour return predicts last half-hour return; Baltussen/van Vliet/Ye 2021 extended to 60+ futures incl. currencies over 40yrs, both report cost-robustness) rather than an internally-invented pattern. London session, sign-only construction faithful to the literature (no magnitude filter), only addition being a stop-loss (papers study pure hold-to-close, not risk management). Tested across 2 pairs, 5 stop widths (20-100 pips), and 2 measurement-window sizes (30/30 and 60/60 min) -- 8 configurations, ALL stayed below PF 1.0 (range 0.67-0.88), win rate never cleared 50%. Likely explanation (see REASON.md): the direct FX evidence in the literature is narrow/crisis-specific (RUB-USD during a financial crisis), the currency evidence that does exist is on FX futures with exchange-defined sessions not spot FX's continuous market, and the effect's own reported predictive R^2 (~1.6%) is weak per-observation -- real in aggregate across many instruments/days, easily swamped by retail costs on one pair's single daily realization. Same 'real but too thin for retail costs' pattern found independently in the scalping investigation, now confirmed at day-trading timescale too. CONCLUSION/meta-finding: this project's actual successes (gotobi, wm_fix_reversal) are anchored to SPECIFIC NAMED institutional flow events, not generic statistical patterns (whether internally-invented technical rules or externally-published academic anomalies studied on different instruments) -- recommend treating specificity-of-mechanism as the primary design principle for future strategies, not just wide search for well-cited ideas. See REASON.md.

day_trading/month_end_fix_reversal.notes: Built per user's 'hunt for another [specific-event strategy]' instruction, after research into month-end institutional FX hedge-rebalancing flows (concentrated in final 2-3 trading days of the month, peaking on the last day around the London 4pm fix -- documented in FX-flow literature). Direct descendant of wm_fix_reversal v2's mechanism (identical fix-window fade logic, its already-locked parameters reused UNCHANGED), with exactly one addition: a pre-specified calendar filter (trade only within TradeLastNDaysOfMonth=3 of month-end). CRITICALLY, no parameter sweep was performed -- this is the first and only configuration tested, a methodologically cleaner evidentiary shape than several earlier 'promising in-sample, failed OOS' results in this project. v1 RESULT: tested on 3 pairs (EURUSD.r, GBPUSD.r, USDJPY) AND as a combined 3-pair portfolio (v1_portfolio/, same pattern as gotobi's), 2018-2022 IS / 2023-2025 OOS. Every single pair IMPROVED out-of-sample, no exceptions: EURUSD PF 1.12->2.21, GBPUSD PF 1.67->2.05, USDJPY PF 1.14->1.42. Combined portfolio ALSO improved: PF 1.25->2.08, max DD 6.48-7.02%->4.39-5.63% (improved, not worsened). Combined-account check (the same one that revealed wm_fix_reversal's hidden correlated-loss problem) resolved FAVORABLY here: 24.2% of multi-pair days see every pair lose together (near-identical rate to wm_fix_reversal's own 24%), but drawdown impact stays mild (only modestly worse than the single weakest pair) rather than doubling, likely because month-end's ~monthly frequency gives correlated-loss days far less chance to cluster into a deep consecutive drawdown than wm_fix_reversal's daily cadence did. Combined trades: 174-176 total across the 8-year window -- still under the 200-trade bar, the one real remaining limitation, inherent to only ~3 qualifying days/month. USDJPY is the weakest of the three pairs (higher drawdown). v1 VERDICT (2026-09-23, Researcher's own genuine recommendation, not user-overridden): ready for live at reduced size, starting EUR/GBP only (leave out USDJPY initially). See STRATEGY.md, VERDICT.md, v1/review.md, v1_portfolio/review.md. day_trading/yen_fiscal_repatriation.notes: Sold USDJPY/EURJPY.r/GBPJPY.r within the final 15 calendar days of March and September (Japan fiscal year-end/half-year repatriation thesis -- Japanese life insurers/pension funds/megabanks reducing FX exposure and adding hedges for balance-sheet reporting; BIS Quarterly Review, Hattori & Shin 2007, practitioner desk research, independently corroborated via live web search post-hoc, see dates.md). Zero parameters swept for v1, following month_end_fix_reversal's methodological lesson. In-sample 2017-2022: USDJPY PF 0.83 (-$317, 120 trades), EURJPY.r PF 0.91 (-$162, 107 trades), GBPJPY.r PF 1.12 (+$293, 110 trades); combined -$185 across 337 trades, all under the 200-trade bar per pair and combined. REVIEWED 2026-09-23 (Researcher): full per-trade reconstruction from all three journals (balance-delta cross-checks matched reported net profit exactly for all 3 pairs). Found the September leg net negative across all three pairs (-$310 combined) and the March leg net positive (+$125 combined) -- matching the citation-strength asymmetry already flagged in dates.md (March much better documented than September). But the March leg's positive total is itself an artifact of one strong year (2019) offsetting one COVID-vol-shock year (2020, stop-outs concentrated in EUR/GBP March legs), not a steady seasonal edge -- the same 'one good year carries the average' pattern flagged elsewhere in this project. Losses otherwise concentrate in identifiable macro/volatility-regime episodes (COVID crash March 2020; the 2021-2022 secular BOJ-ultra-easy/Fed-hiking yen-weakening trend, which directly opposed this strategy's short-JPY-cross thesis for USDJPY two years running, including one window where the spec's own 6-consecutive-loss safety pause fired correctly and truncated trading) rather than random noise. No within-window timing concentration found (last-3-days of the 15-day window did not consistently outperform the full window across years), ruling out 'window too wide' as a motivated fix. No single, causally-motivated refinement survived scrutiny -- dropping the September leg looked promising at first (matches citation asymmetry) but the residual March-only result is itself a small-sample/one-good-year artifact once inspected per year, so locking it would repeat a mistake this project has already made and rejected (wm_fix_reversal v1, overlap_deviation_scalp v1-v4). DISCARDED per this project's house rule (discard rather than sweep parameters when no clear causal fix exists). Meta-finding: a real, well-corroborated, specifically-named institutional flow can still fail to survive backtesting for a reason distinct from intraday_momentum_carry's ('academic effect too generic/thin') -- here the mechanism is real but small relative to the macro-trend/volatility-regime forces that dominate the instrument during the backtest window; citation quality (named participants, concrete calendar trigger) is necessary but not sufficient, it still has to be checked against whether the instrument's dominant macro regime during the test window was fighting the thesis. See v1/review.md and strategies/_graveyard/yen_fiscal_repatriation/REASON.md.

Thesis: the WM/Reuters 4pm London FX fix is the subject of real, named regulatory enforcement (2014-2015 FCA/DOJ/CFTC fines totaling $10bn+ against Barclays/Citigroup/JPMorgan/RBS/UBS for FX desks -- in chatrooms nicknamed 'The Cartel' -- coordinating to 'bang the close', pre-positioning into the 1-5 minutes before the 16:00:00 London fix snapshot), producing a well-documented 'V-shaped' pattern: a directional run INTO the fix, then a partial reversion after. `wm_fix_reversal` (parked) already tested the reversion half (fading the post-fix spike) and found only a thin edge (OOS PF ~1.04-1.06) with a correlated-loss problem across pairs. This strategy deliberately tested the OTHER half never traded in this project: going WITH the pre-fix run (momentum, not fade), entering at 17:59:00 server (15:59:00 London) on an adaptive-threshold-filtered 3-minute pre-fix move (reusing wm_fix_reversal v2's proven volatility-adaptive calibration, not a fixed pip bar) and exiting within 2 minutes (18:01:00 server / 16:01:00 London) -- before the giveback wm_fix_reversal targets has time to develop. Zero parameters swept for v1 (first specified configuration). demo_criteria: min_trades=25, min_days=21. See strategies/day_trading/fix_run_momentum/v1/spec.json and dates.md (2018.01.01-2022.12.31 in-sample / 2023.01.01-2025.12.31 out-of-sample, standard project split). RESULT: all 6 legs (3 pairs x IS/OOS) lost money -- EURUSD.r IS PF 0.72/net -$360.68/132 trades, OOS PF 0.30/net -$524.67/52 trades; GBPUSD.r IS PF 0.52/net -$803.27/149 trades, OOS PF 0.48/net -$561.91/83 trades; USDJPY IS PF 0.18/net -$1,494.99/129 trades (max equity DD 15.08%, right at the project's 15% kill-switch threshold), OOS PF 0.56/net -$396.55/87 trades. 632 combined trades clears the 200-trade significance bar comfortably -- a well-evidenced, not thin-sample, negative result. REVIEWED 2026-09-25 (Researcher, v1/review.md): journal-ledger cross-check (root EURUSD.r IS leg) confirmed the reported PF/net-profit numbers directly from the raw per-trade journal (balance_after ends exactly at 10000-360.68), independent of any summary.csv parsing question. Mechanism check: ~95% of trades in every leg exit via the fixed 2-minute time backstop rather than tagging SL/TP (both sized symmetrically at 1.0x the measured run), so with a near-1:1 payout the outcome is effectively a test of whether price kept moving the same direction for 2 more minutes -- and win rate came in AT OR BELOW the ~50% breakeven point in 5 of 6 legs (as low as 27.1% for USDJPY in-sample), the opposite signature of a momentum-continuation thesis, and consistent instead with mild reversion (read together with wm_fix_reversal's own thin-but-positive result fading the OTHER half of the same V-shaped pattern). Both EA Coder-flagged spec-translation judgment calls (entry_time '18:59:00' vs '17:59:00' contradiction; MinHistoryToAdapt=20 vs wm_fix_reversal v2's actual coded default of 5) were checked and ruled out as explanations for the negative result -- entry_time's 17:59:00 resolution is the only internally-consistent reading with no plausible alternative; MinHistoryToAdapt's effect is confined to at most the first ~20 daily evaluations of each multi-year window, only LOOSENS (not tightens) the entry threshold during that period (opposite direction from the 'starving a valid threshold' concern), and losses show no concentration in the early-warmup trades on spot-check. DECISION: discarded -- a genuine thesis failure (the pre-fix momentum/'banging the close' half of this documented fix flow does not have a retail-detectable edge at 1-minute entry resolution with a 2-minute hold), not a v1-specific implementation bug. No v2/parameter sweep attempted; flipping direction to fade would just re-derive wm_fix_reversal's own (already-tested, parked) mechanism on a tighter window, not a productive next iteration of this thesis. Moved to strategies/_graveyard/fix_run_momentum/REASON.md. See v1/review.md for full detail.
